title: Magnetic fields at the onset of high-mass star formation
question: What are the magnetic field properties (morphology, strength, stability) at the earliest evolutionary stage of high-mass star formation in the starless region IRDC 18310-4?

what.value: N2H+ line width ~0.3 km/s used for sigma_v

evidence.loc: 4.1 Magnetic field strength via Davis-Chandrasekhar-Fermi method
evidence.quote: The one-dimensional velocity dispersion $\sigma_{v}$ is estimated from the width of the N$_2$H$^+$ line measured in this region (cite: beuther2015a).

what.value: Average density n=10^6 cm^-3 and clump line width 1.5 km/s, single-dish column density 1.3e23 cm^-2

evidence.loc: 4.1 Magnetic field strength via Davis-Chandrasekhar-Fermi method
evidence.quote: We estimate $\rho$ assuming an average number density $n=10^6$ cm$^{-3}$ (cite: beuther2013a)

what.value: MAMBO 1.2 mm flux densities (132 mJy in 11'', ~410 mJy in primary beam)

evidence.quote: within the inner $11''$ beam size is 132 mJy

recipe.goal: Image Stokes I, Q, U and combine fields
recipe.method: Mosaic of two fields, natural weighting with small uv-taper; consistency tested using Q/U residuals

recipe.goal: Derive core masses and column densities
recipe.method: Optically thin dust emission from 1.3 mm flux within 4 sigma contours
assumptions: T~15 K, gas-to-dust 150, kappa_1.3mm~0.9 cm2/g (Ossenkopf & Henning thin ice mantles, 1e6 cm-3)

recipe.method: B = sqrt(4 pi rho) sigma_v/sigma_psi with sigma_psi from Stokes Q and U
key_parameters: n=1e6 cm-3, mu=2.8 m_p, sigma_v=0.13 km/s from N2H+ width 0.3 km/s
assumptions: Same sigma_v and n for all sub-regions; frozen-in field, Alfven waves

recipe.goal: Structure function analysis of polarization angles
recipe.method: Fit square of S2(l) with b(l)+a2' l^2 for l>0.5'' and take intercept b(0) as angle dispersion
Alfven velocity, beta~3(sigma_v/sigma_A)^2, M/Phi=7.6e-24 N_H2/B in critical units
assumptions: Alfven velocity in plane of sky equals that along line of sight

evidence.quote: The synthesized beam of these images is $1.01''\times 0.83''$ (PA 89$^o$).
turbulent-to-magnetic energy ratio of $\beta \approx 0.18$ whereas the lower $\sigma_{v}$ for the individual cores would result in $\beta \approx 0.008$
approximately 20-50% of the total flux are recovered by our interferometer observations
